evals.name: backprop-1986-short-landmark
evals.prompt: Summarize this paper for me — I've read the abstract and intro already.
evals.expected_output: A study-guide digest of Rumelhart, Hinton & Williams (1986) that skips the abstract/intro, explains the delta rule generalization and the chain-rule derivation in plain language, covers the family-tree and symmetry-detection tasks as the evaluation, defines the notation, and points at the specific figures worth looking at. Should compress below the 900-word floor because the paper is only 4 pages.
evals.why_this_case: Stress-tests the short-paper edge case, dense 1986 notation, and a paper with no modern-style benchmark table.
assertions: Does not contain a section that summarizes the abstract or the introduction
Contains all seven required sections: header takeaway, Big Idea, Research Questions, Method, How They Tested It, What They Found, Vocabulary, Where to Actually Look
The Big Idea section names the specific prior limitation (no learning procedure for hidden units / perceptron limitation) rather than a generic 'prior work was limited'
Every mathematical symbol that appears in the digest is defined in words at or before its first use
Each glossary entry has both a general definition and a note on how this specific paper uses the term
Contains at least one analogy explicitly marked as an analogy for the core mechanism
The 'Where to Actually Look' section cites at least three specific figures, tables, or sections with page numbers
Numbers quoted in the digest match the paper exactly (spot-check all numeric claims)
Does not use 'novel', 'leverage', 'utilize', 'state-of-the-art', 'significantly', or 'robust' without immediately quantifying against what
Explicitly flags at least one thing the paper leaves unspecified, rather than smoothing over it
Distinguishes what the paper demonstrated from what it claimed or speculated about future work
